Dedicated in loving memory of Jamilla (Elizabeth) Deville.

Welcome

#### A Message from Our Founder

My name is Fawnia, and I’ve seen firsthand what cancer can do, and how deeply it can impact the lives of those we love. I believe we can do more to help people build stronger, healthier lives and give their bodies the best possible foundation before, during and after cancer treatment.

The Melissa Foundation was created from that belief: to empower people with knowledge, resources and support to make healthier choices and live healthier lives at every stage of their journey.

## Blog

URL: https://themelissafoundation.org/blog.html

#### Blog

- By Fawnia

#### What is Cancer?

All cancers originate from our normal cells. Most cancers arise from our interaction with the world in our daily lives. In most cases, cancer can be caused by an emotional trauma, such as losing a child, or by extended emotional stress. Cancer can be caused by issues with teeth, specifically root canals and/or cavitations. These experiences suppress the immune system and provide an opportunistic condition for cancer to grow. Cancer can also be caused by what we drink, smoke and eat. Many cooked (especially microwaved) foods have no live enzymes and few nutrients.

Cancer means the growth of tumors. About 90% of cancers involve a tumor, however not all tumors are cancerous. Cancer also includes a broad range of diseases where tumors are not present. These include lymph system cancers called lymphoma, blood-borne cancers called leukemia, and skin cancers called melanoma.

Cancer is usually a reaction to the lifestyle choices you have made and what has happened to you over the last several years.

96–97% of cancers are caused by a breakdown in cellular communication. If your body’s immune system is healthy enough to fight off all the toxins and free radicals, you don’t get the reaction called cancer. Only 3 to 4% of all cancers come from inherited genes.

More posts are on the way — check back soon.

## Recipes

URL: https://themelissafoundation.org/recipes.html

#### Recipes

Nourish Your Body

#### Juices

#### Why We Love Carrot Juice

Carrots are rich in cancer-fighting nutrients. Carrot juice has more naturally occurring vitamin A, alpha-carotene, and beta-carotene than anything else on earth. One 8-oz cup of raw carrot juice has over 45,000 IU of vitamin A, which promotes liver detoxification, and is healthy, unlike the isolated, synthesized vitamin A found in most supplements.

Carrots also contain another powerful anti-cancer compound called falcarinol, a fatty alcohol (sounds bad, but it’s not). Falcarinol is also found in Panax ginseng, and it has been shown to have antibacterial, anti-fungal, anti-inflammatory, immune-boosting, and anti-cancer properties during laboratory studies, specifically against leukemia and colon cancer.

RECIPE

#### Daily Juice

One serving

- 5 small carrots (peeled)

- ½ beet root (and a few beet greens)

- 1–2 celery sticks

- 1 piece of ginger

More recipes are on the way — check back soon.

## Dedication

URL: https://themelissafoundation.org/dedication.html

#### Dedication

In Loving Memory

#### Jamilla (Elizabeth) Deville

Jamilla was a world-renowned pole artist, performer and teacher whose strength, artistry and warmth touched everyone who knew her.

This website and The Melissa Foundation are lovingly dedicated to my best friend Jamilla Deville, whose life was forever changed by breast cancer. Losing her showed me how deeply cancer impacts not only those diagnosed, but everyone who loves them. Her memory inspires our mission to help people find trusted resources, make healthier choices, and feel empowered to live healthier, fuller lives at every stage of their journey — before, during and after cancer.

For Jamilla, and everyone whose life has been touched by cancer, may we turn loss into hope, knowledge into action, and every day into an opportunity to live healthier.

Fawnia, Founder

#### Give in Jamilla’s Memory

A donation in Jamilla’s name helps someone else find the resources, support and hope she inspired in us. Thank you for keeping her memory alive.

Donate in Her Memory
